title: Training AI models on one value shifted their responses on another
summary: Researchers fine-tuned four language models using examples framed around restraint. On held-out scenarios, all four shifted toward responses labeled collectivist, although individualism was not the training target. The finding describes changes in model responses under a synthetic evaluation.
organization: University of Copenhagen; University of Cambridge

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 front matter, §§3–4, Appendix C.3/C.4 and Tables 7–11

evidence.tested: Adapters and their original models scored the same held-out scenarios, with 1,500 examples per value pole. The shift in relative likelihood was significant in each of the four models under the reported multiple-comparison correction. For restraint-trained adapters, the signed table entries correspond to decreases in the raw high-individualism likelihood margin.
evidence.unknown: The categories and response examples are synthetic operationalizations. The result does not establish model beliefs, human preferences or behavior in deployment.
evidence.ai_role: The study separately fine-tuned four pretrained language models on synthetic examples of individual cultural-value dimensions and then tested labeled response preferences in unrelated dimensions.
